analysis.title: GS Crook - AI Issuance Pulsecheck 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: AI-related debt issuance is a key macro focus while the global bond market is under duress. GS says the sense that investment plans and the issuance behind them are relatively rate insensitive is among the factors weighing on duration risk appetite.
Hyperscalers are not sensitive to the effect their issuance has on long-end yields, because interest expense is a very small portion of their earnings.

Tenor is shortening. In Jan-Jun 2026, 29.9% of hyperscaler issuance was in the 0-5yr bucket. After June the share is 46.4%. Shares in the 20-30yr and greater-than-30yr buckets each fell from 11.7% to 7.1%.

2026 projected hyperscaler issuance is $250bn, with $230bn already completed. 2024 issuance was below $20bn. GS sees risks skewed to the upside because the multi-year build-out and positive sentiment could catalyze more issuance.

GS raised its 2027 hyperscaler gross issuance forecast to $420bn from $400bn. The basis is higher bottom-up CapEx forecasts from GIR equity research and an unchanged assumption that 35% of 2027 hyperscaler CapEx is debt funded.

Hyperscalers are only 40% of the $575bn+ of global gross AI-related debt issuance tracked this year. The rest comes from project finance issuers (IG and HY) funding data centers and chips, and from non-hyperscaler technology and AI ecosystem issuers.
Asset allocators managing total AI exposure are likely to put more emphasis on sector diversification into larger industries removed from the AI theme, such as Banks, Energy and Healthcare.
GS expects the EUR market's share of AI-related issuance to rise. Its year-to-date share is about 5% of gross supply in Europe, versus about 23% in US IG and about 18% in US HY.

Macro implication: AI-funded debt supply raises the sensitivity of long-end yields to debt supply and raises the risk that yields overshoot fair value by a larger margin. GS sees only two things halting this: credibly lower energy volatility and levels, or genuine growth worries.
For equities, the size of 2027+ AI spend means hyperscalers need to show positive ROIC momentum in Q3 earnings, through revenue growth and cloud margins, to maintain confidence in the CapEx cycle.
Hyperscaler credit has been the clear year-to-date underperformer but has outperformed the rest of the credit market since the beginning of August.

AI single-name CDS volumes are up 400% y/y. The universe of liquid single-name AI CDS grew from 4 names last year to 10-12 this year. Notional traded rose from $50-100mm per name per week to hundreds of $ millions per name per day.

In high yield, SoftBank priced an $11.14bn deal to fund its OpenAI investment, the largest non-IG bond sale on record. Paramount Skydance is targeting a possible record ~$12.4bn HY financing this week. PSKY is not AI related but tests the market's ability to absorb back-to-back jumbo deals at tight valuations.
IG index yield is 5.95%, close to 3-year highs, while spreads as a percent of yield are at their lows. GS notes this is the largest source of debate in credit.

sector_views.rationale: GS credit strategy expects allocators to increase sector diversification into larger industries removed from the AI theme, including Banks, Energy and Healthcare, because AI-related supply is heavy across credit.

earnings_insights: Upcoming Q3 hyperscaler earnings: GS says hyperscalers need to show positive ROIC momentum through revenue growth and cloud margins to maintain confidence in the 'generational Capex cycle'.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Close to 3-year highs, while spreads as a percent of yield are at the lows.
Most of this year's hyperscaler funding is done, but risks are skewed to the upside.
Raised from $400bn. Adds long-end supply pressure.

risk_factors: Long-end yields overshooting fair value as AI-related issuance grows, detached from macro drivers.
Upside skew to hyperscaler issuance if sentiment stays strong.
Back-to-back jumbo HY deals (SoftBank, Paramount Skydance) testing demand at tight valuations.
Possible max-escalation in the Middle East, with energy volatility keeping long-end yields under pressure.
Hyperscalers failing to show positive ROIC momentum in Q3 earnings.
vol_and_positioning: Rates selloff has entered a higher-vol phase with a less fundamental flavor, per Will Marshall of GS US Rates Strategy.
AI single-name CDS trading is now liquid in 10-12 names (ORCL, SPCX, AVGO, AMD, NVDA, META, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT among the most liquid), with volumes up 400% y/y.
geopolitical: GS refers to approaching a window of potential max-escalation in the Middle East, and says credibly lower energy volatility and levels is one of two things that could halt the long-end yield pressure.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have outperformed the rest of credit since August, issuance is largely complete for 2026, and Marshall says it is not obvious AI issuance is the specific cause of the rates selloff.
tension_points.bear_case: Rate-insensitive investment plans and debt supply, with $420bn of hyperscaler issuance forecast for 2027, raise the risk that long-end yields overshoot fair value and detach from macro drivers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credibly lower energy volatility and levels, or the emergence of genuine growth worries, would halt or reverse the pressure on long-end yields.

theme_stances.evidence: increase the risk that yields overshoot fair value by a larger margin
